analysis.title: GS Ellinikaki - 10 for the weekend 9 Oct 2026
key_insights: European sovereign stress that began as a France-specific fiscal concern has broadened into a wider European sovereign and rates story, spilling into other bond markets and tightening financial conditions.

Higher oil and inflation keep the risk of another ECB hike alive, but tighter financial conditions reduce the need for further tightening. The ECB has tools to contain disorderly contagion, but fundamental sovereign risk needs a fiscal rather than monetary solution.
GS Europe Economics argues rising sovereign stress, led by France, has tightened Euro area financial conditions enough to reduce the need for further ECB hikes.
GS FX Research sees near-term risks of continued stress and contagion as high, but thinks current credit-based pressures on the Euro are likely nearing their limit.
European Banks sold off this week on long-only degrossing and rising sovereign and rates concerns. GS flows showed sellers in ING, Intesa, StanChart and Lloyds.

GS European Banks estimates a 1% fall in FVPL/FVOCI bond values implies about 15bp of CET1 impact on average, against a sector CET1 of about 14.1%. BCP, HSBC and STAN are most exposed. ALB, BNP and BOI are least exposed.

Tony Pasquariello remains tactically bullish on US equities, citing strong nominal growth, earnings and flows. GS Economics sees only a modest baseline hit to US growth from higher rates, with a more meaningful downside if rates stay elevated.

Clients have re-engaged in Tech, taking Mag 7 net exposure to about 22% of total US exposure on the GS Prime book, the highest since 2022. Semis and Semi Equipment are about 12% versus about 6% at the start of the year.

US Tech was the only sector net bought on the GS Prime book in September, with the largest monthly buying since Feb 2025. Overall net positioning is still low, with US Fundamental L/S (asset-weighted) nets in the 2nd percentile on a 5-year lookback.

GS US TMT team describes a more selective setup into earnings. Debates cover stretched Cyber multiples, whether Internet names can sustain post-earnings follow-through, and the right multiples across AI, Semis and hardware.

Jim Schneider is more constructive on Semis into Q3 after a tricky Q2, citing cleaner positioning and potential estimate upside across SemiCap, compute, analog and storage. The key debate is how much upside remains without clearer 2028+ visibility.

Waller struck a more hawkish tone, signalling two further hikes may be appropriate as geopolitical risks, AI-related price pressures and tariffs cloud the inflation outlook. GS still expects one final 25bp Fed hike in December, with a lower probability of a pause.

Erwan Rambourg initiated Luxury coverage with a Sell on Hermès and Swatch. Investor feedback was cautious, with more negativity than expected on the LVMH and Moncler Buys. He sees 2027 as a turning point for the sector.
LVMH reports Monday after the close.

GS Global Credit Trader is more cautious on EUR HY and USD leveraged loans into 2027. Higher yields and wider HY spreads are increasing refinancing pressure, with higher risk in the left tail of default rates.

GS upgraded Reckitt to Buy on accelerating Core growth (about 5%), margin improvement and a discounted valuation. Consumer Health is described as a 4-5% structural growth category with meaningful consolidation potential. Haleon remains Buy/Conviction List with a new M&A rank.

European Utilities are seeing the datacenter buildout GS expected. The sector owns about 25GW of connection points worth about €20bn today. Integrated DC infrastructure could create about €35bn of incremental value, and the required renewable buildout could drive €100-150bn of investment through 2035.
Solaria has the most upside among European Utilities at about 45%, with PPC, Drax, Fortum and RWE also offering meaningful exposure.

Daniela Costa upgraded Wärtsilä to Buy. The name remains heavily debated on whether looming capacity additions normalise today's tight power market by the end of the decade or simply reflect the scale of the growth opportunity.
